image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) resting on a textured, light-colored ground surface (likely stone or concrete) with scattered dry leaves. The salamander has a glossy black body with distinct, irregular bright yellow spots and patches. Its skin appears wet and reflective. The head is broad with visible parotoid glands behind the eyes. Forelimbs and hindlimbs are visible, showing short, stout digits. The tail extends towards the top left, partially out of focus. There is some gibberish text/watermark in the bottom right corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, broad, and flattened. The characteristic bulges of the parotoid glands behind the eyes are distinct and match the species description.

The body shape is consistent with a robust, cylindrical salamander morphology.

Counting exactly 4 or 5 distinct, blunt, unwebbed digits is difficult due to potential AI artifacting (fusion/melting) at the contact points. The structure looks slightly anomalous.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail extends out of the frame at the top left. The tip is not visible, so the 'rounded tip' criterion cannot be verified.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow spots on the head have a slightly 'painted on' or overly smooth texture compared to the porous, glandular texture of the black skin, lacking the subtle micro-texture variation seen in real amphibian skin.
